title: De Sancto Athanasio, Liber I-II
author: Lucifer
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0180a.stoa004.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's CSEL and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Sciens tu degens sine notitia dei persequeris Athanasium uera tibi dicentem, ex toto amantem deum corde. sic et Achab persecutus Heliam. sed uide exitum Heliae atque inimici eius Achab. Heliam conspice translatum ad amicitias dei perfruendas aeternas, et nune Achab torquetur in exterioribus tenebris.
passages.english: Knowingly, living without knowledge of God, you persecute Athanasius, who tells you the truth and loves God with his whole heart. So too Ahab persecuted Elijah. But see the end of Elijah and of his enemy Ahab. Look at Elijah, carried away to enjoy the eternal friendship of God, while Ahab is now tormented in the outer darkness.
passages.notes: "nune" read as "nunc" (scanning error). "Sciens tu degens sine notitia dei" is somewhat paradoxical ("knowingly ... without knowledge of God"); translated as it stands.

passages.original: nihil enim ueri locuti estis coram me. interea sic uos Arriani superiores poteritis Athanasio inueniri nunc apud deum, quomodo et illi tunc inuenti sunt qui Iob exprobrant. utile est tibi, Constanti, ut per Athanasium domini sacerdotem pro facinoribus tuis sis supplex deo, per ipsum dirigas uota tua, sicuti et illi per Iob; per Athanasium siue per coepiscopos eius des operam salutarem consequi baptismum. ceterum quo uelitis uos torqueatis modo aduersus Athanasium, uos de filiis esse inuenimini, quippe haeretici, illius anguis, colubri refugae desertoris;
passages.english: "for you have spoken nothing true before me." Meanwhile, you Arians will be able to be found superior to Athanasius now before God in just the way that those who reproached Job were found [superior] then. It is to your advantage, Constantius, to make supplication to God for your crimes through Athanasius, the Lord's priest, and to direct your prayers through him, just as those [men did] through Job; [and] through Athanasius or through his fellow bishops to take care to obtain saving baptism. For the rest, in whatever way you wish to twist yourselves against Athanasius, you are found to be among the sons, heretics as you are, of that serpent, that snake, the runaway deserter;
passages.notes: The opening words continue a biblical quotation (God's rebuke of Job's friends) begun in the preceding context. The statement about the Arians being "superior" is ironic.

passages.original: adeo es excors, Constanti auguste, ut nec dictum illud domini, cum haec mandares fieri, potueris reminisci: quid autem uides festucam in oculo fratris tui, trabem autem in oculo tuo non uides ? aut quomodo dicis fratri tuo: sine ut eiciam tibi festucam de oculo tuo, et ecce trabes in oculo tuo, et tunc uidebis eicere festucam de oculo fratris tui. trabem in oculo tuo dicit esse dominus, et audes dicere Athanasio uiro iustissimo: festucam habes in oculo? ille enim nihil horum commisit, quae ei dignaris obicere; contra tu quaecumque diximus es perpetratus, damnate quoties dixisti innocentem.
passages.english: Are you so senseless, Constantius Augustus, that when you ordered these things to be done you could not even remember that saying of the Lord: "Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how do you say to your brother, 'Let me cast the speck out of your eye,' and behold, a beam is in your own eye? And then you will see to cast the speck out of your brother's eye." The Lord says there is a beam in your eye, and do you dare to say to Athanasius, a most righteous man, "You have a speck in your eye"? For he committed none of the things that you deign to charge him with; you, on the contrary, have perpetrated everything we have mentioned, you who are condemned as often as you called the innocent man [guilty].
passages.notes: The quotation is abridged in the text (the clause "first cast out the beam" is missing). The final clause "damnate quoties dixisti innocentem" is elliptical; the sense "called the innocent man [guilty]" (or "condemned the innocent") is uncertain.

passages.original: Ananiae dicitur: ut quid repleuit satanas cor tuum, ut fuisses mentitus spiritui sancto ? et dices, Constanti imperator. quia non repleuerit satanas cor uestrum Arrianorum, ut mentiti fuissetis spiritui sancto manenti in dei ecclesia? ecclesiam etenim conuenisti dicens: deliquit in deum Athanasius; et uidebat spiritus sanctus mendaces animas uestras, sicut uidit et Ananiam ac Sapphiram. uidebat inquam, spiritus sanctus, quando haec fingebatis, quod enim idcirco talia fuissetis commentati circa Athanasium, quo possetis uestram haeresem introducere in ecclesiam, quo possetis apostolicam destruere traditionem.
passages.english: It is said to Ananias: "Why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit?" And will you say, Constantius emperor, that Satan did not fill the heart of you Arians, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit who abides in God's church? For you addressed the church, saying: "Athanasius has sinned against God"; and the Holy Spirit saw your lying souls, just as he also saw Ananias and Sapphira. He saw, I say, the Holy Spirit [saw], when you were fabricating these things, that you had devised such things about Athanasius for this reason: that you might bring your heresy into the church, that you might destroy the apostolic tradition.
passages.notes: Lucifer's Latin is frequently ungrammatical (e.g. the quia-clause after "dices"); the sense has been followed.

passages.original: inueneras homo sapiens colorem aptum fallaciae tuae, quonam modo posses dei oues patri tuo defendere, qui tibi, ut in his demoreris malis, iam illis iaculis quibus Euae et Adae mentes sauciauit cor tuum iaculauit, ad hoc uidelicet, ut in hac temet prauitate constitueret. inueneras, inquam, homo sapiens colorem aptum fallaciae tuae, quonam modo posses dominicum depopulare gregem, dicens: peccauit Athanasius, et idcirco qui illum mecum interemerit erit episcopus; qui insuper habendum censuerit non erit; et qui damnabant Athanasium iungebantur pseudoepiscopis dogmatis tuae Arrianae. si qui tuam metuentes iram hoc egissent, triplex per te homicidam atque sacrilegum incurrebant crimen, siue quod innocentem damnarent siue quod catholici haereticis communicarent et in gregem dei uos lupos intrare sinerent, cum dicat apostolus, idcirco datos pastores, ut omnis daemonum doctrina, quae per uos haereticos et omnes aduersarios ecclesiae profertur, fuisset exclusa atque in ueritate currentes dei serui eo usque mansissent inmobiles, donec ad summam uenirent perfectionem;
passages.english: You had found, wise man, a fitting colour for your deceit, a way you could defend God's sheep for your father, who, so that you might remain in these evils, has already shot at your heart with those darts with which he wounded the minds of Eve and Adam, namely to establish you in this depravity. You had found, I say, wise man, a fitting colour for your deceit, a way you could lay waste the Lord's flock, saying: "Athanasius has sinned, and therefore whoever destroys him along with me will be a bishop; whoever thinks he should be retained besides will not be"; and those who condemned Athanasius were joined to the false bishops of your Arian doctrine. If any did this out of fear of your anger, they incurred through you, murderer and sacrilegious man, a threefold crime: in that they condemned an innocent man, in that as catholics they communicated with heretics, and in that they allowed you wolves to enter God's flock, although the apostle says that pastors were given for this reason: that every teaching of demons, which is put forward through you heretics and all the adversaries of the church, might be shut out, and that the servants of God, running in the truth, might remain unmoved until they came to the highest perfection;
passages.notes: "defendere" (defend God's sheep for your father) seems odd; perhaps a corruption for something like "auferre" or "deferre" (carry off / hand over the sheep to your father [the devil]). "Homo sapiens" is sarcastic. "insuper habendum" may be for "superstitem habendum" (be kept alive) or mean "disregarded"; uncertain.
